title: Prescriptions & Renewals renewal requests and the post-expiry window
content:
Patient Services Center desk guidance for the Prescriptions & Renewals line.

**The rule the desk applies.** A renewal may be requested only for a class that can be renewed at all — an Acute Short-Course Prescription cannot be renewed and needs a new visit — and only through a channel the class allows: a MyLinden portal request where the class allows portal renewal, a phone request where the class allows phone renewal, and always the pharmacy's electronic request. A request that asks to change the dose is not a renewal where the class requires a visit for a dose change.

When a request is logged, the prescription moves from active, or from expired, to renewal requested, and the date the request was received and its channel (pharmacy request, patient portal or phone) are recorded.

**Expired prescriptions.** An expired prescription may be renewed only shortly after it expired. The renewal of an expired prescription is requested no later than the tier's post-expiry window counted from the expiration date. That window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the expiration date, and a request on the last day still qualifies.

| Element | How it is read |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | the expiration date on the prescription record |
| Evidence | the expiration date shown by the system record of this same prescription, read before the request is logged |
| Unit | calendar days |
| First counted day | the day after the expiration date |
| Last counted day | the day whose count equals the class's post-expiry window |
| Request on the last counted day | qualifies |
| Request after the last counted day | does not qualify as a renewal of the expired prescription |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates).**
- A Standard Maintenance Prescription (post-expiry window of 30 days) with an expiration date of 10 June: 11 June is day 1 and 10 July is day 30. A renewal request received on 10 July qualifies; one received on 11 July does not.
- A Monitored Maintenance Prescription (window of 14 days) with an expiration date of 28 February in a non-leap year: 1 March is day 1 and 14 March is day 14, the last qualifying day.
- A class whose post-expiry window is 0 has no counted day after the expiration date, so an expired prescription of that class cannot be renewed through this window.

**Points of judgement.**
- The channel test and the class test apply to every renewal request; the window test applies only to a prescription that has already expired.
- The expiration date is taken from the prescription record, not from what the caller remembers.
